uncited: *   **Empty Tiles:** Tiles with zero cost (empty regions) are rendered first.
*   **Cost Estimation Accuracy:** Tile cost is estimated from a single sample at the tile center in $T_{low}$.
*   **Sorting Granularity:** Sorting individual rays yields poorer performance than sorting tiles.
*   **Visual Transition:** The transition from low to high resolution is visible.
*   **Time Budget Exceedance:** If the time budget is exceeded, rendering stops for that frame.
The next frame resumes from where it left off.
*   **Time Complexity:** The sorting phase is $O(N \log N)$ or $O(N)$ depending on the radix sort implementation, where $N$ is the number of tiles.
This is performed once per interaction session.
The rendering phase is proportional to the number of tiles rendered per frame, bounded by the time budget.
*   **Memory Complexity:** Requires storage for $T_{low}$, $T_{high}$, and correlation maps.
Memory usage is $O(W \times H)$, where $W, H$ are viewport dimensions.
Efficiently utilizes GPU cache by processing tiles.
*   **When to Use:** Mobile and low-performance devices where interactive frame rates are critical and full-resolution rendering cannot be completed in a single frame.
*   **When Not to Use:** High-performance desktops where full-resolution rendering is feasible in one frame, or where visual continuity is more important than interactivity.
The work was motivated by the need to render large medical volume datasets (resolutions $> 512^3$) on mobile devices at full resolution while maintaining interactive frame rates.
